stories.head: True Anomaly banks $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly has successfully raised $190M in a Series C round, bringing its valuation to $1.6B. The funding will bolster its capabilities in co-orbital security and space domain awareness, as the Department of Defense continues to prioritize these areas. This round illustrates a strong pull-through from government contracts, signaling that cash remains king in this sector.
stories.soWhat: Investors are clearly betting that the DoD's appetite for co-orbital security will only grow, which could be a smart move if tensions escalate.

stories.head: Palantir extends TITAN contract by $480M
stories.body: Palantir has secured a $480M extension on its TITAN ground station program, reinforcing its position in government contracts. This extension is part of a broader trend where data analytics firms are increasingly relied upon for national security initiatives. The deal underscores the Pentagon's ongoing investment in advanced data capabilities.
stories.soWhat: Palantir's dominance in the government space is not just about tech—it's about being the go-to partner for data-driven defense solutions.

stories.head: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant clears design review
stories.body: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant for the Department of Defense has successfully passed its critical design review. However, the path to launch remains fraught with challenges, as the company aims to transition from design to operational capability. The DoD's interest in the platform reflects a broader push toward reusable spacecraft.
stories.soWhat: Clearing design reviews is nice, but the real test will be whether Sierra can actually deliver on its promises without losing its shirt in the process.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on Anduril and L3Harris
watchlist.body: Their collaboration on a tactical SDA constellation bid could signal a shift in how defense contracts are awarded.

watchlist.title: NASA's European partnerships expand
watchlist.body: With three new firms added to its satellite data program, NASA might be setting the stage for more competitive bidding in the commercial data space.

watchlist.title: Hypersonic glide-vehicle testing delays
watchlist.body: The continued delays in hypersonic testing raise questions about the U.S. military's readiness in this critical area.

watchlist.title: SpaceX's valuation drama continues
watchlist.body: Investors are still in suspense over SpaceX's valuation and potential secondary offerings, which could impact market sentiment.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
